findings.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/common/admin/admin_base.scss:385 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));" Inlining the same primary/light and secondary/dark derivation in 109 declarations gives 30 component files ownership of one palette algorithm and has already produced four divergent mappings; the strongest rebuttal that selectors need bespoke tuning fails because this change mechanically preserves each existing lightness and only derives its dark counterpart, so one parameterized helper would delete both duplicated arms from every call site without losing selector-specific intent.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss:48 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));" The call-site rewrite stops before the same file's `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification` declaration at line 115, so that category count still derives from `$primary` under dark themes while the rest of the topic-list surface follows the dark palette.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss:291 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));" The light-theme arm changes this topic-metadata link from the pre-change `$primary` lightness of 30% to 70%, making the light theme consume the dark-theme inverse instead of preserving its established color hierarchy.

app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/user.scss:522 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));" The light-theme arm changes `.group-member-info .name` from 30% to 50% and makes it identical to `.title`, collapsing the name/title hierarchy that the original model encoded.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss:102 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));" This reverses the 70%/30% mapping used by the same `.custom-message-length` component at desktop/modal.scss:94, so switching viewports changes the component's theme semantics and darkens its light-theme counter instead of preserving it.

app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));" This replaces the topic-map heading's original 20%/80% mapping with 50%/50% while desktop/topic-post.scss:321 keeps 20%/80%, so the same heading loses its light-theme emphasis and changes semantic hierarchy across viewport implementations.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/_topic-list.scss:115 — [P2][100] "color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);" category-list notification badges still lighten `$primary` in dark themes, so this rendering path remains outside the required `$secondary`-based dark-theme conversion.

app/assets/stylesheets/common/components/buttons.css.scss:77 — [P2][100] "color: dark-light-choose(#fff, scale-color($primary, $lightness: 60%));" primary-button text still selects a `$primary` lightness transform in dark themes, so customized dark palettes retain the exact failure the change is required to eliminate.
